text:
alex: Heads-up — long-run repro on qwen-1.3-mqa: KV memory keeps growing after ~1.5M tokens, ends up ~+700MB vs baseline. Putting this on eng-runtime to triage.

maria: Can you paste the pmap/top/profiler snippet? Is this slab fragmentation or new steady allocations?

alex: quick profiler dump from the run (trimmed):
```
KV pages: allocated 1.22 GB -> 1.94 GB over 90m
fragmentation: 23% (page holes + free slabs)
page_count: 312k -> 498k
perf top: kv_write() 42%, kv_reclaim() 3%
kern_select: chose generic_fallback_kernel for long-seq paths
```

lina: hmm. kern_select choosing fallback generic kernel for sequences > 4096 sounds relevant — fallback path doesn't coalesce page writes, so small writes become new pages instead of merging. Which model config?

alex: model: qwen-1.3-mqa, quant profile: int8-qat, runtime config: `batch_max_tokens=2048` `batch_timeout_ms=5` `rope_factor=4096`. kernel logs show: `kernel_select: fallback due to MQA rope mismatch` around token 1.2M.

kevin: I've seen this pattern when rope scaling mismatch prevents KV reuse: prefix pages are kept but not referenced (ghost pages). Two knobs to try: `kv_sweep_aggressiveness` and `kv_page_signature` coalescing.

maria: can you run with `kv_sweep_aggressiveness=2` and `kv_page_signature=true` to see if coalescing helps?

alex: tried sweep=2 + signature on a shorter run — memory plateaued ~300MB lower but end-to-end throughput dropped ~12%. So it's a tradeoff.

perf-bot: perf/regression alert: qwen-1.3-mqa p99 latency +12% under batcher profile X after enabling aggressive sweep. See: https://perf.redwood/reports/1758888001

lina: That matches the expected tradeoff. Idea: when kernel_select falls back to generic, mark the written pages with `fallback_tag` TTL so sweeper can target them preferentially without global aggressiveness. Also add a fast in-place coalescer that joins adjacent pages with identical signatures.

kevin: plan of action: 1) add quick fingerprint-based coalescer (cheap hash of page content) 2) adapt kernel selection to prefer GQA-optimized kernel when rope_factor > 2048 for MQA variants 3) add `fallback_tag` TTL and targeted sweep 4) run canary perf tests and measure p99/throughput tradeoffs.

maria: :thumbsup: I'll open a telemetry PR to surface `kv_growth_rate`, `kv_fragmentation_pct`, and kernel selection events in the console. Also adding a perf-harness test with `--prefix_reuse=0.7`.

alex: repro command I used: `./run_perf --model qwen-1.3-mqa --seq 8192 --clients 12 --prefix_reuse 0.7 --duration 2h` — dropping here for anyone who wants to reproduce locally.

kevin: FYI I found a small race in `kv_page_write()` where refcount can be leaked if sweep races with writer; I pushed a tiny branch `kv-race-fix` that zeroes that window. That may shave some of the growth too.

lina: I'll pick up the coalescer + fallback_tag patch. Will run a local canary with sweep=1/coalescer on infra perf harness.

alex: thanks — assigning kevin + lina. If we get a canary with coalescer + fallback_tag that keeps memory in check and p99 within +5%, we can roll to canary fleet.

maria: :eyes: will follow tests and post telemetry outputs here.

kevin: quick note — when you test, also include a GQA variant (qwen-1.3-gqa) to compare; I suspect GQA kernel will avoid fallback and show much lower fragmentation.

alex: good call. If anyone else sees similar growth on other long-run jobs, drop logs here and tag @eng-runtime.
